title: Marcos calls for open sea lanes to ensure global energy security
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has called for keeping sea lanes open to ensure the continued flow of global energy supplies during the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community (AZEC) Summit on Tuesday.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has called for keeping sea lanes open to ensure the continued flow of global energy supplies during the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community (AZEC) Summit on Tuesday.
He also emphasized the need for enhanced information-sharing among oil-producing and oil-consuming countries, saying stockpiling alone would not be enough to ensure energy security.
"Stockpiling is not enough. Sustainable and enduring energy security demands that oil-consuming and oil-producing nations act in unison," Marcos said in his opening remarks.
"We must deepen information sharing and practical storage arrangements, as well as commit to upholding international law to keep sea lanes open and maintain fair, transparent markets," he added.
The summit is co-chaired by Marcos and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
In her opening remarks, Takaichi said Japan was proposing initiatives to strengthen cooperation on oil stockpiling and power grids.
Takaichi also announced that Japan would establish the Asia Oil Security Task Force, a framework for cooperation on oil procurement during emergencies.

The task force will work with the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA) to strengthen regional energy security, including through information-sharing and oil stockpiling.

The initiative is envisioned as an Asian counterpart to the IEA, which is headquartered in Paris and is establishing a new base in Tokyo. The ERIA, based in Jakarta, is expected to serve as the task force's secretariat.— MCG, GMA News
